title: Swimmer-Distress Drones for Endurance Events
one_liner: A race-day service using thermal-camera drones and AI to spot swimmers in trouble before rescue boats do.
customer: Triathlon, open-water swim and Ironman-style race directors, event insurers, and municipalities running beach swims.
problem: Most triathlon deaths occur in the swim, and safety still depends on kayaks and volunteers scanning choppy water. A study at the 2018 IRONMAN Mont-Tremblant found drones identified 1 of 5 distress events before rescue boats saw them, and human spotters tire.
solution: An operator-plus-software service: one or two drones with visible and thermal cameras track the swim course, AI flags prolonged stillness, vertical posture or flailing, and alerts go to the rescue coordinator by radio app, with a post-race report for insurers. Later add wearable tags and AED delivery.
why_now: Thermal drone cameras and edge vision models are cheap, FAA rules for wider drone operations are advancing, and open-water race participation is climbing.
revenue_model: $2.5-8k per event, annual series contracts, and insurer-funded discounts.
non_obvious_insight: The pain sits with event insurers and small race directors, for whom one fatality can end the event, so the pitch is loss reduction with data. AI is valuable mainly because it does not get tired.
first_30_days: Buy two drones (about $8k), recruit a licensed Part 107 pilot and a lifeguard consultant, provide free coverage at two local swims to collect labeled footage, and pitch 10 small triathlon directors a $1.5k pilot.

title: Verified Pay Receipts for Truck Driver Hiring
one_liner: Drivers upload settlement stubs and AI turns them into the true, receipts-backed pay per mile and per hour away from home for every carrier, sold as a hiring credential and as income proof for lenders.
customer: Honest mid-size carriers (50 to 1,000 trucks) that pay $6k to $15k to hire each driver and can't prove their pay claims are real. Secondary buyers are mortgage and auto lenders (bank-statement and non-QM brokers) who serve drivers.
problem: Recruiter ads say 'up to 75 cents a mile, $100k+' but realized pay is often 20 to 35% lower after unpaid or practical-versus-paid miles, unpaid detention, chargebacks and deductions. Driver turnover at big truckload carriers runs near 90%, and job ads are so discredited that honest carriers can't stand out. Drivers whose pay is structured as tax-free 'per diem' also see a low W-2 and get denied mortgages after 20 years of work. Estimates say the English-proficiency and non-domiciled CDL crackdowns will pull 214,000 to 437,000 drivers (5 to 12% of CDL holders) from the supply over 2 to 3 years, so carriers are competing harder for domestic drivers.
solution: A mobile app where drivers photograph settlement stubs and pay statements. AI extracts paid miles, deadhead, detention, deductions, per diem and time away from home, and computes effective take-home per hour on the road, not just per mile. Public carrier pages show verified figures such as '312 verified drivers, median $0.61 per paid mile, $17.40 per hour away'. Carriers that look good pay for a 'Verified Pay' badge and applicant funnel. A second product builds an income-verification packet from stubs and deposit statements for lenders. Fraud controls include stub-format checks, duplicate detection and consistency with driver-reported miles.
why_now: Shrinking driver supply from the 2025 to 2026 English-proficiency out-of-service enforcement (proposed codification rule published Aug 10, 2026) and the Feb 2026 non-domiciled CDL restrictions means cost-per-hire is rising. Vision-model OCR of messy pay stubs is now cheap and accurate. Truth-in-leasing rules already require itemized settlements, so the raw material exists.
revenue_model: Carrier subscriptions of $500 to $3,000 a month for the verified page, analytics and applicant funnel. Lender referral fees of $300 to $1,000 per funded mortgage or truck loan. Free for drivers, which keeps the data supply growing.
non_obvious_insight: Drivers don't compare carriers by ads, they ask in the truck-stop lot 'what do you actually clear?' The only artifact they trust is a pay stub. The honest carriers are the ones locked out of trust, so they are the natural paying customer. The true unit of pay is dollars per hour away from home, because 14-hour clocks, detention and unpaid waiting eat the mileage math. And per-diem income structures are a hidden mortgage trap that a stub-based income packet can fix.
first_30_days: Post in trucker Facebook groups, Reddit and TikTok: 'Upload your stub, see your real rate vs. what your carrier advertised.' Aim for 500 stubs in 30 days. Publish a 'State of Real Pay' report ranking 20 named carriers and pitch it to trade press (Overdrive, CDLLife, FreightWaves). Sell 'Verified Pay' badges to the 5 mid-size fleets whose numbers look best, and sign one bank-statement mortgage broker for lender leads.

title: Blue Tarp Index: Adjuster Ground Truth for ILS
one_liner: A subscription that sells cat-bond and reinsurance investors what veteran field adjusters can see in the first 10 days after a disaster, before any model or carrier report exists.
customer: ILS funds, cat bond trading desks, reinsurance-broker analytics teams, and hedge-fund or equity analysts covering Florida, Gulf and California-exposed carriers. Roughly $30k-$120k per year per team.
problem: Post-event loss estimates swing wildly (Milton was pegged anywhere from a few tens of billions up, and cat-bond implied-loss marks moved daily) and settle slowly. The cat bond market is now about $65.6B outstanding after a record $17.6B of H1 2026 issuance, and most of that capital marks to modeler guesses and carrier press releases. Investors have no structured ground truth for the variables that decide severity: how many roofs really failed, whether demand surge is 10% or 40%, and whether contractors can staff repairs at all.
solution: A vetted panel of 60-150 independent veteran cat adjusters files 10-minute standardized mobile observations on publicly visible conditions only: blue-tarp density per 100 roofs on sampled blocks, roofing debris and dumpster counts, mystery-shopped contractor and tarp-crew quotes ($/sq, lead times), hotel and RV occupancy, and adjuster deployment density. Outputs are an event dashboard, a 'Blue Tarp Index' and a demand-surge index within 72 hours to 10 days, a weekly note, and paid expert calls. Hard rule, reviewed by counsel: no claim-file, policyholder or carrier-confidential information, only public observation and market pricing, aggregated and anonymized.
why_now: Cat bond and ILS capital hit records in 2026, with over $120B of ILS capacity, so more money is exposed to event-loss uncertainty than ever. Claims-adjuster employment fell about 21% year over year through May 2026 as carriers automate, which leaves a large pool of experienced people who need income and are cheap to recruit. The very quiet 2026 Atlantic season (no hurricane until at least Sept 11) gives a scrappy team time to build and back-test before the next event. Wildfire, hail and flood events also count as live tests.
revenue_model: Annual subscription tiers ($25k signal-only, $60k with expert calls, $120k+ bespoke event coverage), per-event pay-per-call expert sessions, and paid retrospective studies. Adjusters get $75-$150 per completed field report plus a revenue share pool. Gross margin is high because the data is field labor, not infrastructure.
non_obvious_insight: Models price wind and exposure, but severity in the real world is set by contractor capacity: how many roofers, tarp crews and drying crews physically exist within 200 miles. An adjuster feels that constraint on day 4 because they cannot get a tarp crew to a house, and nobody in finance measures it. Tarps are also what the policy pays for first, so their density is a fast, visible proxy for claim frequency. The hypothesis is testable by back-testing against Helene, Milton and the LA fires.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 laid-off or semi-retired cat adjusters from cat-adjuster Facebook groups, adjuster forums and LinkedIn. Draft the observation protocol and a counsel-approved compliance memo. Run a retrospective 'what we would have told you on day 7' study on Helene/Milton and the Jan 2025 LA fires using panel memory, public imagery and contractor pricing archives. Publish a free sample note, send it to 15 ILS portfolio managers and 5 broker analytics heads, and aim for 2-3 paid pilots ($15-25k) that include the retro study as a deliverable, with the first live test on spring 2027 hail or a wildfire.

title: Parametric Insurance on Colorado River Shortage
one_liner: Insurance and hedges that pay out when official Colorado River operating triggers or reservoir projections cross agreed thresholds, sold to large industrial and municipal water buyers.
customer: Chip fabs, data centers, breweries, resorts, master-planned developers and municipal utilities that depend on Lower Basin supplies. Buyers pay premiums, and reinsurance and capital-markets funds take the risk.
problem: Powell plus Mead storage is about 36% and 95% of the basin is in drought. About $1.4T of annual activity is exposed, yet businesses cannot hedge water-supply or rate shocks except by capex. Until this year the rules were too ambiguous to write a contract against.
solution: Start with a Lower Basin water-supply risk index and term sheets, sold to muni-bond investors and industrial water buyers. Then build a parametric product that pays on published operating triggers or reservoir projections, funded through a surplus-lines or Lloyd's partner with an experienced weather-risk insurer. Payouts fund contingency supply, recycling or trucked water.
why_now: The Aug 2026 Record of Decision set the 2027-2036 operating framework, converting political ambiguity into published rules that a contract can reference. Capital-markets investors seek risks uncorrelated with catastrophe.
revenue_model: Premium (a percentage of limit), analytics licensing before any policy is issued, and a share of fund fees.
non_obvious_insight: The ROD makes the river's rules legible, which is the precondition for a derivative. The correlated hydrology scares traditional insurers, but that is exactly what non-catastrophe capital wants to hold.
first_30_days: Build the risk index from Reclamation's public 24-Month Study projections and reservoir data. Interview 10 fab, data-center and utility water managers on what loss they fear. Approach one weather-risk reinsurer and one ILS fund. First revenue comes from analytics sold to bond funds and industrial users.

title: Payday-Shaped Pix Automático Cadence for Low-Income Billers
one_liner: A layer on top of Brazilian gateways that designs the recurring-debit cadence (weekly, biweekly, payday-aligned) and consent options at enrollment, so small billers stop losing all-or-nothing monthly debits.
customer: Small Brazilian businesses billing low-income or irregular-income payers on a recurring basis: neighborhood ISPs, small gyms, neighborhood schools, discount-card clinics, motorbike-rental fleets for delivery couriers (to validate first), and insurance or consórcio sellers. They pay 10-15% of incremental collected revenue.
problem: Pix Automático collects the full amount or nothing, with no partial debits. Retries are limited to 3 in 7 days and only if the payer consented. The payer can cancel or edit the mandate up to the eve of the debit, and the mandate cannot change frequency or amount ceiling after authorization. Meanwhile 83.9 million Brazilians were in negative credit standing in August 2026, a record. Monthly lump debits collide with irregular income, and small merchants still chase payers by hand every month.
solution: At enrollment, quote cadence from the payer's income rhythm (weekly for app-paid couriers and informal workers, biweekly for 'vale' and salary splits, monthly for salaried payers) and create the correct mandate with retries-consent and, optionally, credit-line consent. A WhatsApp 'pre-debit rescue' 48-72 hours before each charge lets the payer confirm, move the date to just after payday, pause, or split into a new mandate, instead of silently cancelling in the bank app. Built as an API layer over a gateway that already exposes the retry policy, such as Asaas. Reports per merchant show debit success rate, cancellation reasons and recovered revenue.
why_now: Pix Automático launched in June 2025 and adoption is compounding. Companies had to be able to offer it from 1 Jan 2026, and it is far cheaper than cards and has no chargebacks. About 60% of low-income Brazilians lack credit cards, so account-debit is the only recurring rail for that segment. Most tooling so far is generic dunning, not cadence design.
revenue_model: Performance-based: 10-15% of incremental collected revenue versus the merchant's baseline, or a flat R$149/month for merchants who prefer subscription. Later a per-debit micro-fee and a marketplace of payer-side 'payday buffers'.
non_obvious_insight: The frequency is locked at authorization, so cadence is an irreversible, high-leverage decision at signup, and nobody optimizes it. Because partial collection is not allowed, the only way to fit a low-income payer's cashflow is to change the shape of the debits, not to chase them afterwards. Evidence: PagBrasil reports +182% transactions and +181% new users quarter over quarter from Q4 2025 to Q1 2026, and a coffee subscriber cut churn 25.2% and cost 50% versus cards (https://www.pagbrasil.com/blog/recurring-payments/automatic-pix-2026/). Serasa reported 83.9 million negativados in August 2026 (https://www.shipay.com.br/inadimplencia-no-brasil-como-melhorar-cobrancas/). Rules on no partials, 3 retries in 7 days and cancellation until the day before are at https://celcoin.com.br/articles/vale-a-pena-pix-automatico/ and https://docs.asaas.com/docs/faq-2. The mandate 'cannot change the frequency' and 60% of low-income Brazilians lack cards (https://www.pymnts.com/news/payments-innovation/2025/pix-automatico-debut-opens-brazils-recurring-payments-market-to-millions/). Small billers describe the monthly grind: 'Todo mês alguém precisa lembrar o cliente, mandar mensagem, enviar chave Pix, cobrar boleto atrasado' (https://www.alfadenegocios.com.br/2026/08/pix-automatico-para-pequenos-negocios.html).
first_30_days: Days 1-3: Confirm in the BCB spec which recurrence periodicities are permitted (weekly and biweekly are assumed, not yet verified) and the per-debit fee, since more frequent debits cost more per charge. Fall back to monthly with payday-aligned dates plus split mandates if not. Days 4-15: Build a thin layer over the Asaas API and a WhatsApp pre-debit rescue flow. Recruit 10 merchants from a single vertical, ideally neighborhood ISPs or courier motorbike-rental fleets, through their ERP user groups and Facebook groups. Days 16-30: Run a split test (monthly vs payday-aligned vs weekly) on new enrollments, report debit success and cancellations, and sign the first 3-5 performance-fee contracts.

title: Payee-Verification Network for the Live Music Business
one_liner: A shared, industry-vouched directory of who is really entitled to be paid in the touring economy (agencies, promoters, venues, production vendors), checked before every deposit wire.
customer: Independent and mid-size booking agencies, regional promoters, festivals, tour accountants and business managers, and production, trucking and staging vendors. Starting wedge is 50-200 person agencies and promoters that wire 50% artist deposits.
problem: Live touring runs on large advance wires: artist-guarantee deposits, production advances and vendor prepayments, with banking details passed through PDF contracts and email across dozens of small counterparties whose bookers, agents and accountants change often. That is ideal business-email-compromise territory (US BEC losses $3.05B in 2025 per FBI IC3), and now voice clones make 'the agent called to change the account' credible (a vendor report claims 680% year-over-year growth in voice-deepfake attacks). The FBI fund-freeze process recovered 58% of attempted funds but only when victims act fast, and each bank sees only its own side. Europe's mandatory Verification of Payee on euro transfers (from Oct 2025) checks name against IBAN only inside the euro zone, and the US has nothing similar, while tours mix currencies and countries.
solution: Verify each entity once (KYB, identity of authorised signers, bank account proven by micro-deposit or open banking) and publish signed payment instructions. Settlement spreadsheets and accounting tools check payees against the network before a wire is released, via a plug-in for spreadsheets, Slack and common accounting software. Any change of banking details triggers out-of-band, multi-party confirmation (agent, manager and accountant, never a reply-to email), with a 24-72 hour cooling-off for first payments. A bank hot-line handshake speeds recall and freeze on suspected misdirection. Each deal also generates a shared verbal code phrase to defeat cloned-voice calls.
why_now: IC3's 2025 numbers, AI-enabled scam operations earning about 4.5x more than others (Chainalysis, per briefing), and cheap voice cloning. Live Nation's $25.2B revenue and its arena buying show the sector's money is growing and consolidating, so more wires move through more small counterparties. EU Verification of Payee shows regulators' direction but leaves the cross-border and hybrid gap open.
revenue_model: SaaS of $99-499/month per verified entity. Per-payment verification fee of $2-5 or 0.02-0.05% for high-value wires. Bank and payments-provider licensing. Insurance partnerships where crime/cyber insurers discount premiums for network members.
non_obvious_insight: Payments-fraud vendors sell to banks and large corporates, but the live industry is thousands of small counterparties whose trust is relationship-based. The relationship graph (who is the legitimate agent, manager or accountant for whom) lives in people's heads, so the moat is a graph the industry vouches for itself. Once most deposits flow through the network, an unverified change-of-details request becomes an obvious red flag.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 mid-size booking agencies or tour accountants (the people whose wires get hit). Give them a free payment-instruction registry as a spreadsheet plus Slack or Chrome extension. Capture verified bank details for their top 100 counterparties. Run a consented voice-clone fire drill to create urgency. Charge $199/month per agency by day 60 and approach two insurers for premium-discount pilots.

title: Receipts-Only Reviews via Open Banking
one_liner: Reviews that only people who provably paid can post, with the payment verified through open-banking data and only merchant, amount band and month disclosed.
customer: UK and EU independent restaurants, salons, tradespeople and clinics (verified-review widget and profile subscription), with lenders, insurers and marketplaces as later data buyers.
problem: Trustpilot removed 4.5M fake reviews in 2024 and was fined by Italy in Mar 2026 for failing to verify authenticity. The FTC rule and UK consumer law ban fake reviews, and no platform can verify offline purchases. Merchants cannot prove their reviews are real, and review sites sell services to the businesses they rate.
solution: The reviewer links a bank through an open-banking account-information partner (such as TrueLayer or GoCardless). The app reads one transaction and produces a selective-disclosure attestation (merchant, amount band, month), then posts. Merchants get a '100% paid-customer reviews' widget and structured-data markup. Reviewers get neutral, sentiment-independent cashback funded by merchants.
why_now: Fake-review enforcement is intensifying (FTC warning letters Dec 2025, Italy's Trustpilot fine Mar 2026), the AI-generated review flood is growing, and AI shopping agents ingest reviews as trust signals. Open banking now has enough UK users to make linking a normal action.
revenue_model: GBP 19-49 per month merchant subscription, API and data licences to lenders and marketplaces, and float on cashback funding.
non_obvious_insight: The referee problem vanishes when the proof comes from the bank, not the platform. A review site that sells to the businesses it rates can never be trusted, but a receipt cannot be bought.
first_30_days: Sign 30 independent restaurants in one UK city, put a QR code at the till, and build on an open-banking partner's sandbox. Launch with local press as 'the review site you cannot buy'.

title: On-Demand Human Witnesses for Scrap and Recycled Claims
one_liner: A network of trained, insured, credentialed ex-auditors and QA people who can be dispatched within 24 hours to physically inspect scrap lots and witness recycled-content claims, producing tamper-evident signed reports.
customer: Remote buyers of bales and scrap lots (PET reclaimers, black-mass and tungsten buyers, brokers, traders). Brands making recycled-content claims, and their insurers and lenders. The buyers' own AI purchasing agents consume the reports through an API.
problem: PET bales trade at a record-low 1.44 c/lb while food-grade supply is called constrained, which points to a quality-tier mismatch nobody can see without inspection. Generative AI makes photos, scale tickets and certificates trivially forgeable. Traditional inspectors have minimum fees and multi-day lead times. Mass-balance claims are contested and no standard exists. California's AB 2253 (claim substantiation) was vetoed, leaving brands exposed to litigation. EU rules banning generic green claims (Directive 2024/825) began applying on Sept 27, 2026.
solution: Recruit displaced auditors, QA analysts, supply-chain and compliance staff and give them a one-day protocol course on bale and scrap specs. Dispatch them to open and grade bales, XRF-screen metals, seal loads, witness weigh-outs and attend recycled-content production runs. They use a capture app with device attestation and signed provenance, and every report is machine-readable. Visits cost $95-250 versus $800+ for traditional inspection. Each witness builds a portable, scored reputation, so the credential becomes their asset.
why_now: AI forgery capability is now cheap and widely known, so document trust is falling. The BIS Aug 27 rule adds recordkeeping for black mass and tungsten scrap. Brands need substantiation now that the EU rules apply. Agentic procurement needs verifiable physical inputs. The supply of trained auditors and analysts is growing because of AI-driven cuts.
revenue_model: Per-inspection fee split about 60/40 with the witness. Monthly claim-assurance subscriptions for brands ($1-3K). API and report-verification fees for buyers' agents. Later, a quality-tier index of bales sold to the market.
non_obvious_insight: When AI can fake any document, the scarce commodity is a credentialed human who was physically present. The scrap trade runs on thin margins and unverifiable quality claims, so cheap, fast human presence beats expensive certification. AI displacement supplies the witnesses at the same moment it destroys trust in paperwork.
first_30_days: Pick one corridor with several bale or e-scrap buyers and offer 20 discounted bale inspections to three remote buyers. Recruit and train 10 witnesses (ex-QA and audit). Build the capture flow on existing attestation and C2PA tools. Publish a first bale-quality report from the results.

title: Personalized Cancer Vaccines for Dogs
one_liner: Falling costs of tumor sequencing, neoantigen prediction and small-batch mRNA make a bespoke cancer vaccine per dog plausible; start with the sequencing and design report oncologists can order today.
customer: Veterinary oncologists and university teaching hospitals, and owners of dogs with newly diagnosed aggressive cancers (hemangiosarcoma, osteosarcoma, mast cell tumors, lymphoma).
problem: Owners of dogs with cancer are offered chemo, surgery or nothing. The briefing notes about 80% of dogs with lymphoma never get IV chemo, and only one oral option has recently arrived. Owners will pay for hope, but experimental individualized therapies are inaccessible, and existing genomic panels mainly match small-molecule drugs rather than designing a vaccine.
solution: Phase 1: tumor-normal sequencing, neoantigen ranking and a clinician report in about 10 days, sold to oncologists. Phase 2: under a vet-school client-owned-dog research protocol, produce an individualized mRNA vaccine through a small-batch CDMO, with regulatory strategy set with USDA veterinary biologics and FDA CVM.
why_now: Sequencing runs at a few hundred dollars per genome, open protein and neoantigen prediction tools are strong, small-batch mRNA manufacturing is contract-accessible, and human personalized-vaccine programs are running. Loyal's conditional-approval progress shows vet regulators will work with novel therapies.
revenue_model: $1.5-3K per sequencing report, $10-25K per vaccine research-protocol fee, and licensing of the genomic dataset to human-oncology developers.
non_obvious_insight: Dogs are an excellent human-cancer model: spontaneous tumors, shorter timelines, owner-funded and lighter regulatory burden than humans. The paid 'hope' market is outside insurance, and the tumor-normal dataset itself is a licensable asset.
first_30_days: Partner with one vet-school oncology service and a sequencing lab. Enroll the first 10 dogs for sequencing-only analysis at cost. Sign an MOU with a small-batch mRNA CDMO. Submit a research protocol and recruit through oncologist referrals and owner communities. Individualized therapy remains experimental, so set expectations accordingly.

title: Copyright-Registration Autopilot for AI Settlements
one_liner: Monthly bulk US copyright registration and an evidence vault for creators, so they are eligible when AI settlements and claims open.
customer: Newsletter writers, podcasters, photographers, illustrators and indie musicians, plus small publishers and labels, most of whom have never registered a work.
problem: In the Anthropic authors settlement (Sep 2025), only works with timely US registrations qualified, and new music and news suits (for example UMG and Sony against Suno, per the brief) follow the same logic. Registration also gates suing at all and statutory damages. Most independent creators skip it because of fees and friction, which puts them at the back of every claims line.
solution: OAuth into Substack, Beehiiv, Ghost, Bandcamp and portfolio storage. The service assembles the right group registrations (short online literary works, photographs, unpublished works, albums), files them with the Copyright Office, tracks registration numbers and deposit copies, and keeps a tamper-evident vault of first-publication evidence. A claims desk alerts users when a settlement or class definition matches their registered works. Has an attorney review the workflow.
why_now: The 2025-2026 AI settlements and suits made registration status the gating asset. Creator demand for anything that pays them from AI is high, and the Suno-Warner settlement shows deals are landing.
revenue_model: $19-39/month plus pass-through Copyright Office fees, a $99 first-year catch-up batch, and an optional 10% of recovered settlement payouts through the claims desk.
non_obvious_insight: Class-action money goes to the paperwork-ready. For an AI-era creator, registration status may be the most valuable and most neglected asset, and the boring gate is where a subscription business sits.
first_30_days: Partner with a copyright attorney to design the workflow. Pilot with 50 newsletter writers and 20 illustrators from creator communities, using a free 'AI-claims readiness audit' as the lead magnet.

title: Chip-to-Billet Solid-State Metal Mini-Mills
one_liner: Turn aluminum machining chips directly into billet, rod or wire by friction extrusion, with no remelting, first as a tolling service and then as on-site micro-mills.
customer: Aerospace, defense and precision machine shops with segregated 6061 and 7075 chips, plus extruders and AM wire makers who want recycled content.
problem: Machining chips sell for a fraction of ingot value and are remelted with real melt loss and energy. Aerospace buy-to-fly waste is huge, and domestic aluminum is exposed to tariffs and supply shocks.
solution: Solid-state processing (friction or shear-assisted extrusion, developed at national labs) consolidates single-alloy chips into bar or wire feedstock, preserving alloy chemistry. Phase 1 is a tolling service: ship chips in, get billet back. Phase 2 is a leased on-site mini-mill.
why_now: Tariffs on imported aluminum rose to 50% in mid-2025 and defense and aerospace capacity is stretched. Solid-state processes moved from lab demos toward pilots, so a first product now exists.
revenue_model: Tolling fee per pound returned, then equipment lease plus per-pound fee, plus recycled-content premiums.
non_obvious_insight: Melting destroys the metallurgical history. Chips from a single-alloy shop are effectively pre-alloyed, so solid-state consolidation captures value that a remelt discards.
first_30_days: Partner with a national lab or press builder. Run sample consolidations on chips from 3 shops and test tensile properties. Sell pilot lots to 2 extruders. Apply for AFWERX or SBIR support.

title: Celebration-of-Life Halls in Closed Churches
one_liner: Lease shuttered churches and run them as turnkey memorial venues sold at checkout by direct-cremation providers and hospices.
customer: Families holding a memorial after a cremation ($2.5-6k per event). Referral partners are low-cost and direct-cremation providers, hospice social workers and estate attorneys.
problem: Cremation was about 62% of US dispositions in 2024 and is projected to hit ~82% by 2045. Direct cremation is the fastest-growing category, but it unbundles the ceremony. Families end up planning a memorial themselves in a restaurant or backyard, funeral-home chapels are being sold off, and nobody runs the day: music, slideshow, live-stream, seating, catering, display of ashes.
solution: Take a long lease or lease-to-own on a closed church. Denominations often discount buildings for gentle uses and restrict bars or clubs, so a memorial hall is an easy yes. Install AV and live-streaming for far-away family, and hire a bereavement-trained coordinator. Add a photo-to-memorial-video service, caterer partnerships and a wall of memory. Sell it as a $2,900 'Add a Celebration of Life' package on the partner's checkout page. The other six days a week, book weddings, concerts and community events. Columbarium niches are a phase-two option after legal review.
why_now: Direct-cremation startups have marketing reach and no physical venues. Congregations keep closing after COVID. Live-stream AV and AI-assisted photo-to-video tools are now cheap enough for a two-person team to run.
revenue_model: Event package fee (venue, AV, coordinator; $2.5-6k). Catering margin. Memorial video upsell (~$400). Referral revenue share to partners. Weekday event rentals. Later, columbarium niches with perpetual-care fees.
non_obvious_insight: The direct-cremation revolution unbundled the ceremony and nobody rebundled it. A sanctuary already has the emotional weight and acoustics, and resale restrictions make sellers accept a low price for a respectful use. Idle-week rental income turns a grief business into a resilient one.
first_30_days: Contact diocesan and conference property offices about 5 closed churches for month-to-month special-use agreements. Pilot 3 events at cost-plus with 2 direct-cremation providers and 2 hospices. Collect testimonials and photos. Stand up a booking page and a bereavement-friendly phone concierge.

title: L-Band Radar Watchdog for Small Levee Districts
one_liner: Turn free NISAR L-band radar into monthly, engineer-stamped settlement and seepage alerts for the small local districts that own most of America's levees.
customer: Reclamation, levee and drainage districts (California Delta and Central Valley, Iowa/Illinois/Missouri/Arkansas drainage districts) and owners of small high-hazard earthen dams and irrigation canals. Budgets are $50k to $2M a year, run by a board plus a part-time manager.
problem: Grass-covered earthen levees lose coherence in C-band InSAR (Sentinel-1), so cheap remote settlement monitoring never worked on them. Districts rely on annual walk-through inspections by volunteers or consultants. Failures are catastrophic, and grant, subvention and insurance paperwork demands documented condition history that most districts lack.
solution: A pipeline on NISAR L-band (about 10 m, 12-day repeat, which sees through vegetation) plus Sentinel-1 and soil-moisture change. It produces per-levee-mile maps of slumping, settlement and unusual wetness (seepage proxy). Alerts go to a partner licensed geotechnical engineer, who signs a one-page condition letter. The district attaches that letter to state levee-subvention and federal rehabilitation-program files, insurer renewals and board minutes. The dashboard is secondary; the stamped trigger is the product.
why_now: NASA/ISRO began releasing NISAR L-band data free through ASF DAAC on July 20, 2026 (acquisitions from June 17, 2026; full science record due by end of 2026). Tens of thousands of levee miles are locally owned, and nobody had L-band time series at this cadence before. Whoever starts the baseline now owns the longest history.
revenue_model: Subscription of $3k to $8k a year per district, tiered by levee miles. Add $1.5k to $4k per engineer-stamped event report. Later, portfolio-level data licences to flood insurers and reinsurers, and to state agencies that fund many districts.
non_obvious_insight: The radar data is free and commoditizing, so the data is not what the customer buys. They buy a defensible, professionally signed trigger that unlocks grant money, satisfies insurers and shifts liability. The moat is the engineer-of-record relationship, local ground truth and a baseline archive that starts accumulating today.
first_30_days: Process Sentinel-1, ALOS-2 and the first NISAR stacks over one Delta island or Iowa drainage district with a known past slump, to show a retrospective catch. Sign a geotech firm as engineer of record. Offer 5 districts a free baseline map and a $1.5k pilot, pitched at levee-district association and flood-board meetings. Aim for 2 paid pilots by day 30.

title: Swarf Stabilization for New US Magnet Plants
one_liner: Hazmat-grade stabilization, transport and recycler routing for the pyrophoric NdFeB grinding swarf that new US magnet plants will produce in tonnes.
customer: New and expanding US sintered-magnet makers and independent magnet grinding shops, who pay per-kg handling. Recyclers and re-melters are the downstream buyers.
problem: US magnet capacity is ramping (MP Materials broke ground on a Texas magnet campus in Feb 2026 on a DoD-backed deal). Machining and grinding turn a large share of sintered NdFeB, often 20-30%, into oil-wet, self-heating swarf and sludge. It is hard to classify, ship and store, so it drifts to overseas buyers or hazardous-waste disposal.
solution: An inerting and oil-immersion protocol, DOT-compliant packaging for self-heating solids, permitted storage through a partner, and routing to domestic recyclers or re-melters. It comes with a mass-balance certificate that lets the magnet maker claim recycled content to defense and EU customers.
why_now: Trace the chain: DoD equity and DPA-style support create new US magnet plants, which create swarf, which becomes a fire and compliance problem with no dedicated service. EU rare-earth recycled-content obligations phase in 2028-2032, and recyclers such as Cyclic Materials are funded and hunting for clean feed.
revenue_model: Handling fee per kg, plus a revenue share of recovered oxide or alloy value from recyclers, plus an annual compliance retainer.
non_obvious_insight: The near-term rare-earth urban mine is inside the factory. Swarf is clean, known-composition and available in tonnes before any end-of-life magnet wave arrives.
first_30_days: Call EHS heads at the 5 new or ramping magnet plants and 10 grinding shops. Offer a free swarf audit to quantify tonnage and value. Line up a hazmat-permitted storage and transport partner and one recycler offtake. Run a first pilot shipment.

title: Verified-Guardian Credential Built on Childcare Centers
one_liner: Start as a custody-aware pickup and consent app for childcare centers, then turn those institutions into issuers of privacy-preserving 'verified parent of a child aged X' tokens that apps pay for.
customer: First: childcare centers, camps and youth orgs (SaaS at $50-150 per site per month). Later: app stores, game studios and platforms (per-attestation fees), and state agencies.
problem: Parental-consent laws (Ohio, Florida, Texas and others) need a verified parent, but credit-card or ID checks prove adulthood, not parenthood. OS vendors will supply age attestation but not guardian relationships. Meanwhile childcare centers and schools already verify guardian-child relationships, custody orders and authorized pickup, and that verification is not reusable.
solution: Phase 1 is a check-in and pickup app with ID and liveness verification for guardians, custody-order parsing, an authorized pickup list, and e-consent for photos, trips and immunizations. Phase 2 lets the center vouch, through zero-knowledge or selective-disclosure tokens, that an adult is a verified guardian of a child in an age band, without revealing identities to apps.
why_now: Consent laws took effect in mid-2026, OS-level age signals exist (California, Texas), and age-verification breaches have made 'verify once, store nothing' attractive. Zero-knowledge age-proof libraries appeared in 2025 (from memory), and the brief identifies guardian and consent workflows as the gap OS vendors won't fill.
revenue_model: Center SaaS ($50-150 per site per month) now, and per-attestation fees ($0.10-0.50) from platforms later, with revenue share to issuing centers.
non_obvious_insight: Identity startups verify people, but the missing primitive is verifying a relationship. The institutions that already do it (childcare centers with custody paperwork) form an unmonetized, fragmented long tail.
first_30_days: Interview 20 center directors about pickup disputes and custody paperwork. Build an MVP with QR pickup and a custody-document vault. Sell 10 centers at $79 a month. Integrate an ID-verification vendor for guardian checks and sketch the token format with a privacy engineer.

title: Parcel-Level Rebuttals to Wildfire Insurance Scores
one_liner: Evidence packs showing a coarse satellite-derived wildfire score is wrong about one specific lot, filed under new statutory appeal rights.
customer: Independent insurance agents and HOAs or fire-safe councils in Colorado and California whose clients face nonrenewal or surcharges. Insurers' appeal desks are a later buyer.
problem: Colorado HB25-1182 (in force since July 1, 2026) makes insurers disclose the parcel's score, credit documented mitigation and offer an appeal. California AB 75, operative July 1, 2026, gives notice and dispute rights over aerial-imagery nonrenewals. But 'owners still have to prove their case', and many wildfire models lean on roughly 30 m fuel layers and stale imagery that misclassify irrigated, gravel-scaped or recently cleared lots.
solution: For each parcel, pull the disclosed model inputs (fuel class, vegetation density, distance to wildland) and overlay multi-date 15-50 cm satellite imagery showing vegetation change, roof material and clearance, plus dated homeowner photos. Produce a regulator-format rebuttal pack with a ranked list of cheap fixes, and give agents a dashboard that scans their whole book for likely score errors. The real edge is a growing database of which input errors insurers concede.
why_now: Both disclosure-and-appeal regimes went live in July 2026 and insurers' appeal desks are unprepared. Commercial constellations, including 30 cm Pelican and Vantor archives, plus 15 cm HD, have made high-resolution archives cheap. Regulators in CT, NH and PA say imagery alone is insufficient, and NY has a pending bill.
revenue_model: $149-$299 per parcel via agents. $10-$25 per parcel per year for HOA book scans. About $60 per appeal from insurers for standardised evidence intake.
non_obvious_insight: Wildfire scores are averages of coarse layers, so the cheapest way to change a score is often to fix an input error rather than harden the house. The resolution gap between 30 m models and 30 cm imagery is systematic, so a win on one lot tends to generalise to its neighbours and compounds into a book-level lever for agents.
first_30_days: Pick the Colorado Front Range. Recruit 5 independent agencies with 200+ WUI clients each, plus 2 HOAs. Run the first 50 score disclosures at a $99 pilot price per file, and track appeal success rate as the marketing asset.

title: Worker-Ownership Succession for Home Care Agencies
one_liner: A specialist shop that helps retiring home-care agency owners sell to their caregivers via an ESOP or worker co-op, plus a shared back office for the converted agencies.
customer: Owners aged 58-72 of $2-15M revenue home-care agencies with no successor. CDFI lenders and employee-ownership funds are financing partners.
problem: Reimbursement is squeezed (a 1.3% aggregate cut for CY2026, with a -3.0% temporary adjustment still in place), private-equity money goes to software and big platforms, and even UnitedHealth had to divest 164 Amedisys locations. Small owners have no buyer, while agencies lose 77-80% of caregivers a year.
solution: A conversion shop: valuation, readiness (licensure and payer change-of-ownership rules), structure (S-corp ESOP, worker co-op or employee-ownership trust), financing (seller note plus CDFI or SBA), and a two-year ownership-culture program (caregiver equity, profit sharing, scheduling voice). Converted agencies share a back office (payroll, billing, EVV, recruiting).
why_now: Boomer owners are retiring into a weak sales market after the 2026 rate squeeze, and the workforce shortage means the workforce is the scarcest asset. Cooperative Home Care Associates in the Bronx shows the model works.
revenue_model: Transaction fee of 3-5% of deal value, $8-15k a month back-office fees, and a small share of network EBITDA.
non_obvious_insight: In a business where turnover is the profit killer, the best buyer for a struggling agency is the workforce itself. Ownership is a retention tool, and the exit-plan angle sells to owners who don't care about culture.
first_30_days: Work with a state home-care association to get 20 owner conversations. Sell five $12k ownership-readiness assessments, line up a CDFI lender, and target first LOI within six months.

title: CRA Technical-File Compiler Built Into CI
one_liner: A GitHub/GitLab app that assembles the Cyber Resilience Act technical documentation, Annex I evidence and draft declaration of conformity from every release, so compliance is a build artifact rather than a consulting project.
customer: Product-security leads and CTOs at connected-device makers with 20-300 engineers (smart home, industrial IoT, e-bikes, wearables, network gear, EV chargers) selling into the EU. Not the GRC team.
problem: CRA reporting duties began 11 Sep 2026, full application is 11 Dec 2027, and fines reach EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover. Manufacturers must keep versioned technical documentation (risk assessment, design, vulnerability handling, test evidence, SBOM), for roughly ten years or the support period. GRC platforms produce policy evidence, SBOM tools produce component lists, and consultants charge tens of thousands per product line for a file that goes stale on the next release.
solution: The app reads the repo, CI logs, SBOM (SPDX/CycloneDX), threat-model files and test results, then maps them to the Annex I essential requirements and vulnerability-handling duties. It posts gaps as pull-request comments ('no secure-update mechanism documented'). Each release yields a signed, timestamped technical-file bundle (PDF plus machine-readable), a declaration-of-conformity draft, a support-period statement and a diff from the previous release.
why_now: Reporting is already live and full application is 15 months away, so products in design today are locking in the choices that determine compliance cost. Harmonised standards are still arriving, so teams need structured evidence now rather than a finished standard to tick off.
revenue_model: SaaS at $1,500-6,000/month per product line, EUR 5-15k onboarding, and referral revenue from test labs and notified bodies.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume Vanta/Drata-style GRC platforms will absorb the CRA. But the CRA is product regulation: the evidence lives in Git, CI and design docs and must be regenerated each release. That is a developer-tool, bottom-up sale to engineers, not a compliance-officer sale.
first_30_days: Interview 15 device makers via CRA meetups and open-source foundations working on CRA. Build a CLI that ingests a CycloneDX SBOM plus a small cra.yaml and emits a skeleton technical file. Run three paid pilots (EUR 3-5k) that produce each firm's first file, and publish the Annex I checklist as open source to draw inbound.

title: AI-Guided Feline Heart Screening by Technicians
one_liner: Handheld ultrasound with AI probe guidance lets technicians capture heart clips on cats, with remote cardiologist over-read making HCM screening a routine add-on instead of a referral.
customer: General-practice clinics (senior and pre-anesthetic cats), breeders of at-risk breeds, and shelters; later insurers.
problem: Feline hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is common and often silent until clot or heart failure. Screening needs a cardiologist's echo, which is scarce and costs a few hundred dollars, so most cats are never screened. Cat households are growing (53M) and the vet workforce is not.
solution: Existing vet-priced handheld probes, a guidance app that prompts standard views and rejects poor clips (trained on cardiologist-labeled data), and a board-certified over-read within 24 hours with next-step recommendations. Sold as a 'senior cat heart check' and a breeder program.
why_now: AI acquisition guidance for novices has been proven in human echo, handheld ultrasound is cheap, vision models are strong, and remote reading is a way to stretch scarce cardiologists while techs take on more scope.
revenue_model: $60-90 per over-read, probe leasing at about $199 per month, and breeder program fees.
non_obvious_insight: The product is not AI diagnosis; it is AI acquisition guidance so a technician can collect usable images. The scarce resource is the cardiologist's time, so pooling over-reads creates the leverage, and the resulting longitudinal dataset improves guidance and screening protocols.
first_30_days: Sign 1-2 board-certified cardiologists on a per-read basis. Equip 5 clinics with handheld probes and run 100 screening scans. Measure the share of diagnostic-quality clips, then sell a $99 senior cat heart check.

title: SOC 2 for Rent-Pricing Algorithms
one_liner: An independent audit and continuous-monitoring attestation proving an operator's revenue-management tool uses lawful inputs and real human decisions.
customer: Multifamily operators (5,000-100,000 units) using RealPage, Yardi or Entrata-style pricing in ban or enforcement jurisdictions, defendants under consent decrees needing monitors, and their insurers and lenders.
problem: Pricing tools are now legal liabilities: New York State (Dec 2025) and Berkeley ban them, San Diego levies $1,000 per violation and a UDR class action was filed, private settlements exceed $500M, and Pinnacle signed a decree Sept 4 with Camden the lone unsettled original defendant. Vendors named in suits cannot credibly certify themselves, and operators cannot prove where prices come from.
solution: Audit data lineage (any nonpublic competitor inputs, data age), analyze auto-accept and override rates and human-decision documentation, map jurisdictional exposure, and issue a signed attestation with quarterly evidence reports. License the tooling to monitors of consent decrees.
why_now: Decrees can require compliance officers and monitors, city bans are multiplying, and insurers and lenders are beginning to ask for proof.
revenue_model: $20-60K annual attestation per operator, monitor tool licenses, and insurer or broker referral arrangements.
non_obvious_insight: Independence is the product, and vendors in litigation cannot sell it. As with SOC 2 in cloud, the standard will belong to whoever writes v1 and gets insurers and lenders to accept it. Acceptance rates are the observable that plaintiffs and monitors will use.
first_30_days: Draft a 'Rent Pricing Compliance Standard v0.1' with antitrust counsel. Offer a free exposure scan to 30 operators and sign three paid design partners at a $10K discount. Approach two monitor firms and a D&O broker.

title: Second-Opinion Price Check for Vet Estimates
one_liner: Upload a photo of a vet estimate and get a line-by-line price benchmark and a list of questions to ask your vet within 24 hours, from vet-tech reviewers, for $19-29.
customer: Pet owners facing $500+ estimates (about 95M US households own pets), plus pet insurers and employers as a later benefit channel and independent clinics as a fair-price badge buyer.
problem: Vet services inflation ran 5.5% YoY in April 2026, and household spending at vets rose almost 4x as fast as spending on pet food and treats (about 1%). BofA Global Research says veterinary pricing is rising faster than wages, so many households delay wellness visits, dentistry and diagnostics. 25-30% of US veterinary practices, and roughly 75% of specialty clinics, are now owned by corporations or private equity (AVMA 2024, cited by BofA), which can erode competition. Pet insurance uptake stays low, and younger and lower-income households are pulling back on pet spending. When an owner is holding an estimate for a sick animal, there is no neutral benchmark.
solution: A mobile-first upload flow. OCR reads the estimate, and licensed vet techs (not diagnosing, just reviewing) compare each line item to regional price ranges, flag bundled or optional items, note which items are typically deferrable versus urgent, and give a short script of questions for the clinic. Every review adds anonymized line-item prices to a growing regional price database, which becomes the moat. Later features are a 'fair-price verified' badge for independent clinics and a payment-plan and generic-drug price check.
why_now: The data now shows a sharp split: sticker prices climb while pet food and store spending stalls, meaning owners are squeezed specifically at the vet. Private-equity consolidation is a live news story, and owners can share estimate photos easily. Pet-insurance carriers face rising claim costs and have an incentive to fund price transparency.
revenue_model: $19-29 per review, $9/month for unlimited pet-family plan, B2B licenses to insurers and employers ($1-3 per covered pet per month), and clinic subscriptions for verified fair-price badges ($99-199/month per clinic).
non_obvious_insight: The pain is not that pet care costs money, it is information asymmetry at the moment of an estimate, and the same dynamic is what made medical-bill advocacy a business for humans. Vet inflation is running roughly 4x pet-food spending growth, and owners are already responding by deferring care rather than shopping around, so the demand is for a fast, trusted benchmark, not another directory. Evidence: BofA Institute, 'The price of pet parenting has gone off leash,' 18 May 2026 https://institute.bankofamerica.com/economic-insights/pet-ownership-costs.html and full PDF https://institute.bankofamerica.com/content/dam/economic-insights/pet-ownership-costs.pdf (vet inflation 5.5% YoY, vet spending growth about 4x pet-store, 25-30% of practices corporate or PE owned, 95M pet households, $158B spend, deferred care). Legal caveat: state veterinary practice acts restrict diagnosing without a client-patient relationship, so reviewers must stay in price and question-generation territory.
first_30_days: Hire two contract vet techs at an hourly rate. Launch a landing page and post in owner communities and Reddit pet-cost threads with 'send me your estimate and I'll benchmark it free' to collect the first 100 estimates. Build the price table by hand in a spreadsheet, then charge $19 from review number 30. Approach one pet-insurance MGA or employer-benefit broker with the first regional benchmark chart. Target 100 reviews and 30 paid by day 30.

title: Independent-Pricing Ledger for Algorithmic Antitrust Risk
one_liner: A neutral logbook beside revenue-management software that proves humans set rents and room rates independently, and doubles as the underwriting file for algorithmic-collusion defense cover.
customer: Mid-size multifamily operators (2k-25k units), hotel groups and self-storage and student-housing operators using shared-pricing algorithms, plus their antitrust counsel and D&O or defense-cost carriers.
problem: The DOJ's RealPage settlement (Nov 2025) bars use of competitors' nonpublic data and alignment of prices. California and New York banned algorithmic rent-setting in Oct 2025. Class actions continue against landlords, not just vendors. Liability turns on whether users set prices independently or rubber-stamped a pooled tool, and on data provenance. Operators cannot produce that evidence, and carriers will not underwrite defense costs without it.
solution: A light ledger fed by exports or APIs from Yardi, RealPage, Entrata, Duetto and similar tools. It records recommended versus adopted price, override reason codes and data-provenance flags. It produces a quarterly 'independence attestation' reviewed by an outside economist, includes a simulator showing the revenue cost of overriding (often small), and packages an underwriting-grade file for defense-cost cover. Design it under counsel's privilege from day one.
why_now: Enforcement plus new state and city laws hit in late 2025 and 2026, and the settlements set monitoring expectations. Mid-market operators are the next wave of defendants and cannot afford bespoke audits. Insurers are simultaneously narrowing AI and antitrust cover.
revenue_model: $1.50-4 per unit per year (about $6-20k for a 5k-unit operator), $10-25k per year for economist attestation, and 10-15% of the defense-cost premium placed.
non_obvious_insight: The legal variable is not the algorithm's accuracy but its acceptance rate and data provenance, and both are just logs. Evidence must exist before the subpoena arrives. The ledger also becomes the first actuarial dataset for algorithmic-antitrust risk, which no carrier has.
first_30_days: Partner with an ex-DOJ or FTC economist and an antitrust boutique. Build CSV-only ingestion for two property-management systems. Approach 10 mid-size operators through a National Apartment Association state affiliate and their counsel. Sell a $7.5k 'independence audit' of the last 12 months of pricing decisions as the entry product, delivered services-first.

title: Patent-Grade Variant Maps for Biologics
one_liner: Pooled-screening service that generates the sequence-function data biologics patents now need after Amgen v. Sanofi, plus a mirror-image design-around report for companies facing sequence claims.
customer: IP counsel and patent boutiques at antibody and protein biotechs, biosimilar and biobetter developers, and mid-size biotechs working in crowded target classes.
problem: Trend chain: Amgen v. Sanofi (2023) killed functional genus antibody claims unless the specification enables the full scope. Patents therefore shrink toward sequence-specific claims backed by data. Counsel typically has data on 20-50 variants. Meanwhile cheap DNA and AI design make thousands of function-preserving variants easy to produce, so both breadth-by-data (offense) and design-around (defense) become experimental problems that no one packages.
solution: Offense: pooled display or mammalian screening of 10^4-10^6 designed variants with NGS readout, delivered as patent-ready sequence-function tables and generalizations (which CDR positions tolerate what) to support broader claims. Defense: search patent sequence claims, compute identity against claim thresholds, design function-preserving escapes and validate the top candidates in a pool. Sold through IP counsel, not legal advice.
why_now: DNA is no longer the cost: Weizmann built 2.5 billion antibody fragments on phage for EUR 38,000 of DNA. Zero-shot design tools generate variants at scale. Post-Amgen enablement pressure has had three years to bite, and law-firm commentary is now explicitly tackling AI and enablement.
revenue_model: $40-150k per patent family for offense work, $8-25k per FTO or design-around candidate, and subscriptions for boutiques.
non_obvious_insight: With cheap DNA and pooled assays, 'enablement by data' becomes a commodity for whoever runs the experiment. Patent breadth turns into a function of wet-lab throughput rather than lawyer cleverness. The same machine that broadens your claims also narrows a competitor's, so buyers exist on both sides of every thicket.
first_30_days: Sign 3 IP boutiques as design partners. Build a claim-matching tool on public USPTO and EPO sequence listings. Offer 10 free FTO scans. Contract a pooled-display partner. Price one paid offense pilot with a biotech preparing a continuation filing.

title: Abandoned Property and Tenant-Death Response Crew
one_liner: A per-event service that handles the legally dangerous moments landlords dread most, such as a tenant who vanishes leaving belongings or a tenant who dies alone, with statutory clocks, next-of-kin outreach and documented disposal.
customer: Property managers and small landlords, who pay per event ($400 to $1,500). Later customers are eldercare social workers, hospital discharge teams, medical examiners' offices and estate attorneys, who all need someone to close out a residence properly.
problem: A 400-unit manager deals with a handful of abandonments a year and one to three tenant deaths. Each event is handled ad hoc. Abandoned-property statutes vary by state, with notice periods, itemized inventory rules, value thresholds and sale-or-storage requirements. One mistake, such as tossing a bin or entering too early, creates conversion or wrongful-eviction liability. With a death, no one has authority to enter or dispose of belongings, the estate has no representative yet, next of kin are unknown or hostile, rent accrues, and the unit sits dark for months. Hoarding and biohazard situations make it worse. There is no standard vendor, so the maintenance supervisor is doing legal and emotional work no one trained him for.
solution: A regional response team with a state-specific statutory workflow. Step one is intake and legal-clock software, which starts the required notice dates, produces the notices, photo-inventory and valuation report and stores it as evidence. Step two is next-of-kin and estate-representative outreach, with sensitivity training for the caller. Step three is secure storage in a partner facility, then sale, donation or disposal exactly as the statute allows, with receipts. Step four is coordinating hoarding or biohazard remediation and the final walk-through for deposit accounting. A companion product is an e-signable lease addendum letting tenants (especially seniors) name an emergency contact and authorized person for post-death property disposition, in the states where that is permitted. That builds a pipeline of pre-authorized cases and makes each later event simple.
why_now: The number of renters aged 65+ living alone is growing fast, which means more deaths in rental units and more hoarding and welfare issues. Several states have recently added or modernized tenant-designated-contact and abandoned-property procedures, though rules remain patchy. Software-only proptech has ignored this because it is field work. Junk-removal and storage marketplaces have made the physical logistics cheap to subcontract.
revenue_model: $400 to $1,500 flat fee per abandonment or death event, plus pass-through storage and disposal cost at a 15 to 25% markup. Optional readiness subscription ($1 to $2 per unit per month) for PMs, covering the lease addendum, templates and priority response. Eldercare and estate-attorney referral relationships add a second channel.
non_obvious_insight: Ordinary landlords fear the eviction. Experienced managers fear the abandonment and the death, because the law in those cases punishes shortcuts, no procedure exists, and the loss (months of rent plus liability) is bigger than a normal eviction. Nobody sells the service because each case is small and the required knowledge is a stack of 50 state statutes. That fragmentation is the moat: once you have playbooks for a handful of states, competitors cannot copy them quickly.
first_30_days: Pick one state and read the abandoned-property and death-of-tenant statutes closely, ideally with a landlord-tenant attorney on a fixed-fee review. Build the notice, inventory and timeline templates. Sign three PMs (find them through the local NARPM or apartment association) to a pilot: 'call us on the next event, first one at cost'. Line up a junk-removal company, a storage unit partner and a biohazard remediation subcontractor. Publish a simple blog page and a landlord-association talk titled 'What to do when a tenant dies or disappears' to start inbound.

title: Original-Recording Music for Memory Care
one_liner: A playlist and licensing service for memory-care communities that matches each resident's favorites to the exact original master, and flags re-records, sound-alikes and AI covers that streaming catalogs are now full of.
customer: Memory-care and assisted-living operators (activity directors), adult day centers, home-care agencies and board-certified music therapists. Adult children pay for a family tier.
problem: Personalized music is one of the few low-cost tools that reaches people with dementia, but it depends on recognition of a specific, familiar recording. Streaming catalogs are riddled with 'greatest hits, re-recorded' versions, sound-alike compilations and now AI tracks. Deezer says over 50% of daily uploads are fully AI, and Sony has asked for 135,000+ impersonations to be removed. Understaffed activity directors cannot tell a 1966 master from a 2019 re-record, and facilities also carry public-performance licensing exposure.
solution: Intake asks a resident or family for songs, era, and where they danced or heard it. The software resolves each song to the original ISRC and audio fingerprint of the label master, rejects re-records, covers and AI-flagged tracks, and produces a device-ready playlist with the public-performance license bundled. Families can add human-made voice messages and personal recordings, stamped as verified human. Staff get a one-page 'response log' to note which tracks got reactions.
why_now: AI-track volume passed human uploads on Deezer in July 2026. Spotify, TIDAL and Bandcamp now label, demonetize or ban AI music, so machine-readable authenticity signals exist for the first time. Memory-care occupancy sits near a record 90%, the 80+ population is growing fast, and blood-test diagnosis pushes more families into post-diagnosis coping tools.
revenue_model: $99-199 a month per community, $12 a month for a family tier, and a per-seat licensing bundle where labels or collecting societies agree to a senior-living rate. Later, a B2B API for music therapists.
non_obvious_insight: In this setting the active ingredient is the exact recording rather than the song, and that is a provenance problem. The 'AI flood' harms the most vulnerable listeners because it degrades the catalog a caregiver assumes is authentic. The first pilot should test the hypothesis that covers and re-records underperform originals.
first_30_days: Build a resolver on public metadata (MusicBrainz, Discogs, label catalogs) and a fingerprint service. Offer a free 'playlist audit' to 10 memory-care communities and to Music & Memory-certified programs. Track staff-logged resident responses for original versus re-record and publish the result as your credibility asset.
